blocks.text: Lima: Art, Tradition and the Larco Museum

provenance.rationale: Combine the approved Day 2 Lima, Art and Tradition and Larco Museum wording into a concise itinerary heading.

blocks.text:
At 09:00, begin the half-day “Art & Tradition” city tour. Start at Parque del Amor in Miraflores, overlooking the Pacific Ocean, then enjoy a panoramic view of Huaca Pucllana, the ceremonial centre of ancient Lima. In San Isidro, visit Huaca Huallamarca, a pre-Inca temple.

Continue to the historic centre, including the main square, Government Palace, City Hall, Cathedral and Santo Domingo Monastery, with its seventeenth-century corridors and courtyards.

After the tour, transfer to a restaurant for lunch (not included).

At 14:00, transfer to the Larco Museum. At 14:30, begin a curator-led visit lasting approximately two hours. Housed in a mansion built over a seventh-century pre-Columbian pyramid, the museum displays an extensive collection of pre-Columbian artefacts, including a celebrated exhibition of erotic ceramics.

Between 19:30 and 20:45, a Spanish-speaking driver will transfer you to Rafael restaurant. Dinner is not included. Return to the hotel afterwards.

blocks.text: Iquitos and the Beginning of the Amazon Expedition

provenance.rationale: Align the itinerary title with the approved Word heading Day 3 Iquitos Amazon and the Aqua Expedition programme.

blocks.text:
Transfer to the airport for the 45-minute flight to Iquitos. Here the group AQUA EXPEDITION programme begins, introducing you to the Amazon rainforest.

The Amazon rainforest covers about 40% of South America across nine countries. The Amazon River rises in the foothills of the Andes in Peru and runs east for some 6,400 km to the Atlantic Ocean. During the rainy season, rising water floods large areas of forest and waterways become the main way to explore this landscape.

This vast region supports exceptional biodiversity, with at least 40,000 plant species, 427 mammal species, 1,300 bird species, 378 reptile species, more than 400 amphibian species and around 3,000 freshwater fish species.

The following days take you along the river and into Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve. As the river rises, small boats can navigate flooded forest channels, allowing you to observe wildlife and riverbank scenery from the water.
